text:
None of the candidate hypotheses is supported as the main hypothesis of the study's abstract:

- **Hypothesis 1** proposes systematic vertical and lateral variations in trace element ratios (Ti, V, Ce) and stable isotopes ($\delta^{18}\text{O}$, $\delta^{26}\text{Mg}$), modulation by deformation and metamorphism, and analysis via LA-ICP-MS, EPMA, and U-Pb geochronology. Aside from noting low-Ti ($< 1\text{ wt\%}$) magnetite and Ti enrichment in the iron-poor caps and hydrothermal aureole, none of these specific tracers, processes, or methods are present in the abstract.
- **Hypothesis 2** attributes deposit formation to mixing of immiscible Fe-rich melts with metasomatic fluids derived from underlying sedimentary basement at $300\text{--}600^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{--}3\text{ kbar}$, with specific salinity, pH, $\Delta\text{FMQ}$, cooling rates, and $\text{Pb}$–$\text{U}$–$\text{Th}$ signatures. In contrast, the abstract states that *silicate* melts interact with oxidized $\text{P}$-$\text{F}$-$\text{SO}_4$-bearing sedimentary rocks to generate Fe-rich ultrabasic melts, and that hydrothermal fluids are *exsolved* from the melt during massive magnetite crystallization rather than derived from basement devolatilization.
- **Hypothesis 3** states that Fe-rich immiscible melts interact with P-rich ironstones at $\pm 800\text{--}1000^\circ\text{C}$ and $\pm 300\text{--}500\text{ MPa}$ and proposes mass spectrometry of $\text{Pb}$ isotopic ratios ($^{206}\text{Pb}/^{204}\text{Pb}$, $^{207}\text{Pb}/^{204}\text{Pb}$, $^{208}\text{Pb}/^{204}\text{Pb}$). The abstract instead describes silicate melts interacting with oxidized $\text{P}$-$\text{F}$-$\text{SO}_4$-bearing sedimentary rocks to promote separation of Fe-rich melts, and contains none of those specific P–T ranges or $\text{Pb}$ isotope details.
- **Hypothesis 4** presents a highly specific quantitative model for El Laco involving mantle liquid immiscibility ($1\text{--}2\text{ GPa}$, $1200\text{--}1300^\circ\text{C}$), AFC with Paleozoic P-rich ironstones, specific $^{206}\text{Pb}/^{204}\text{Pb}$ and $^{87}\text{Sr}/^{86}\text{Sr}$ thresholds, partition coefficients, and host andesite. None of these site-specific or quantitative claims appear in the abstract, which outlines a general model for magnetite-(apatite) systems across deep to subaerial crustal environments.

CHOICE: NONE
